# Anomaly Detection in Large-Scale Cloud Systems

## An Industry Case and Dataset

This research paper explores the use of AI-driven anomaly detection for secure identity and access management in cloud platforms. It discusses the traditional machine learning approaches and basic artificial neural networks used for detecting anomalies. The paper also highlights the importance of fairness and bias mitigation in AI-driven monitoring systems.

### References
- [Anomaly Detection in a Large-scale Cloud Platform](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.10966)
- [AI-Driven Anomaly Detection for Secure Identity and Access Management in Cloud Platform](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/iel8/11076601/11076605/11076807.pdf)
- [Anomaly Detection and Early Warning Mechanism for Cloud Service](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.07407)
- [Anomaly Detection in a Large-Scale Cloud Platform | Semantic Scholar](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Anomaly-Detection-in-a-Large-Scale-Cloud-Platform-Islam-Pourmajidi/0e74f3215673f20927ae52c56f770d9959357ecf)

## Anomaly Detection in a Large-Scale Cloud Platform

This paper designed and implemented an automated monitoring system for the IBM Cloud Platform that utilizes deep learning neural networks to detect anomalies in near-real-time in multiple Platform components simultaneously and can be leveraged by the IBM Cloud services to implement the layered architecture. The relations between the services are represented graphically in Figure 1. The data collection and analysis pipeline is distributed over the two composite layers of one and two. Data wrangling and filtering happen in layer one, while the data analysis and anomaly detection happen in layer two.

### References
- [Anomaly Detection in a Large-Scale Cloud System: An Industry Case and Dataset](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.09047)
